skill.name: why-did-this-post-flop
skill.description: Work out why one specific post underperformed, by separating whether it was not seen, seen and skipped, or read and ignored. Use when someone asks why a post did badly, why nobody engaged, why a post they were proud of went nowhere, or wants one post diagnosed. Do not use it to review a whole account, and do not guess at numbers the person has not given you.
skill.summary: Diagnose whether one post failed through low distribution, weak engagement, or a mismatch between engagement and the intended outcome.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.value_statement: A weak post can fail because it was not distributed, was seen and skipped, or asked for the wrong response. This skill uses available metrics, account baselines, and post structure to identify the likeliest failure and recommend one next change.
actual_capabilities: Separates distribution problems from content and engagement problems.
Requests post text, impressions, reactions, comments, and reposts before diagnosing.
Compares results with the author’s normal performance when a baseline is available.
Reviews the opening line, specific detail, and reader request.
Accounts for timing, links, reposts, and normal performance variance.
Recommends one prioritized change for the next post.
limitations: It cannot distinguish distribution from content failure without impressions.
It cannot infer missing metrics or replace platform analytics.
A single post cannot establish a reliable long-term trend.
VoiceMOAT data depends on the connector and its latest browser-extension sync.

use_cases.title: Review a disappointing launch
use_cases.description: A solo creator provides one post and its metrics to identify whether reach, content, or the requested action limited results.

use_cases.title: Coach a client on one weak post
use_cases.description: A content consultant uses the post, account baseline, and comparison posts to give a focused diagnosis instead of a full rewrite.

use_cases.title: Investigate a campaign outlier
use_cases.description: A small marketing team compares one underperforming post with nearby posts and chooses one testable improvement.

prompt_templates.title: Basic post diagnosis
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this post using its text and metrics. Separate distribution failure, low engagement after viewing, and a mismatch between engagement and my goal. Post: [paste]. Impressions: [number]. Reactions: [number]. Comments: [number]. Reposts: [number]. Goal: [goal].

prompt_templates.title: Compare with my normal results
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare this post with my usual results and explain what the comparison rules out. Post: [paste]. Post metrics: [paste]. Typical metrics: [paste]. State what is known, what is uncertain, and the single most useful next change.

prompt_templates.title: Review a platform-specific outlier
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze why this post underperformed on [platform]. Consider timing, recency, reply or repost status, outbound links, reach trend, opening line, specificity, and requested action. Use only the evidence provided, then rank the top two explanations.

prompt_templates.title: Use connected account evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the connected post, analytics baseline, nearby posts, and voice insights to diagnose this one underperforming post. Identify the failure type, cite the evidence, distinguish sync limitations from real results, and finish with one high-impact test.

output_examples.input: The post had 42 impressions, two reactions, and no comments. My usual posts receive about 500 impressions.
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: distribution failure. The low impressions explain the low engagement, so rewriting the opening line is unlikely to help first. Check timing, posting history, and whether the post synced correctly.

output_examples.input: The post had 1,200 impressions, 18 reactions, no comments, and normally gets 1,000 impressions with 15 reactions.
output: Diagnosis: the post performed normally for reach and reactions.
The likely mismatch is the goal: it did not create comments.
Next change: ask one specific question that invites a useful response.

output_examples.input: The post reached my usual audience, but people did not engage. The first line says, 'Some thoughts on leadership.'
output_examples.output: Diagnosis: readers likely saw the post but had little reason to continue. Test a specific first line that creates a clear reason to read the next sentence.

best_practices: Provide impressions and a personal baseline before asking for a diagnosis.
State the desired outcome, such as comments, clicks, or qualified replies.
Apply one recommended change and compare the next result with a similar baseline.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a hook rewrite before checking whether the post was distributed.
Do not invent metrics, platform causes, or lessons from missing evidence.
Do not apply six changes to one post when a single test would reveal more.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the post text, impressions, reactions, comments, reposts, and what success meant for that post.

faq.question: Can this diagnose a post without impressions?
faq.answer: It can review the writing, but it cannot separate distribution failure from content failure without impressions.

faq.question: Does it review a whole account?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on one post and uses account context only when you provide a relevant baseline.

faq.question: Can it explain low comments despite good reach?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks whether the post asked for a response and whether the request matched your goal.

faq.question: Can it use VoiceMOAT data?
faq.answer: Yes, when connected. It can use post details, analytics, comparison posts, and voice insights, subject to sync freshness.

faq.question: Will it rewrite my post?
faq.answer: Its primary purpose is diagnosis and one next change. You can request a rewrite after the failure type is clear.
